The accused in this case is tried for an offence punishable under Section 138 of Negotiable Instrument Act 1881, on the complaint of the complainant.

2. The summary of the complainant's case is that:
It is the case of the complainant that, it is a company incorporated under the provision of the Companies Act, 1956 and registered with RBI as Non-Banking Finance Company.
Accused had approached the complainant as co-borrower seeking financial assistance of Rs.8,00,000/- to purchase a motor vehicle and in this regard have entered into a Loan Agreement No.6478196.

But the accused failed to make his periodical payments and against the outstanding amount and issued a cheque bearing No. 597738 for a sum of Rs.3,45,000/- dtd: 16.12.2020 drawn on Ujjivan Small Finance Bank.

As per the accused instructions, the said cheque is presented to its banker HSBC Bank, M. G. Road Branch, Bangalore and after presentation the same has been dishonoured with the reason as "Funds Insufficient" on 28.12.2020.

Thereafter the complainant has got issued legal notice on 25.01.2021 which has been served on 05.02.2021 inspite of which the accused has not made any payment and constrained by the same the present complaint is filed against the accused on 03.03.2021 for the offence punishable U/Sec.138 of N. I. Act.
3.
On filing of the complaint, the cognizance was taken for an offence punishable under Section 138 of N. I. Act and sworn statement was recorded.
As there was sufficient ground to proceed further, a criminal case has been registered against the accused and he was summoned.
The substance of accusation is orally stated to the accused and his plea was recorded.
The accused pleaded not guilty and submitted that he has defence to make.

4. In support of the complainant's case, the sworn statement of the Attorney Holder of the complainant company filed by way of affidavit during the pre-summoning stage is considered as evidence of the complainant company as PW.1 and got marked 08 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.8 and another legal representative of the complainant company is also examined as PW.2 and got marked documents as per Ex.P.9 to Ex.P.12.

On the other hand, accused examined himself as DW.1 and got marked a document as per Ex.D.1 and confronted 03 documents during the course of cross- M/S Mahindra And Mahindra Financial ... vs Eshwarappa on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34486734/

sentences.text: 5. Heard the arguments on both sides.

6. The points that arise for my consideration are:
1. Whether the Complainant proves that accused has committed an offence punishable under Section 138 of N. I. Act 1881?
2. What order?
7.

My answer to the above Points is as follows:
 Point No.1: In the Affirmative,
 Point No.2: As per final order,
 for the following:
 REASONS  FACTS OF THE CASE :
8. POINT No.1:

The present case is filed by the complainant company through its legal representative and he examined as PW.1 by filing his affidavit evidence in lieu of oral evidence,
wherein, he has reiterated the entire averments made in the complaint.

In support of his evidence,
PW.1 has produced the document as per Ex.P.1 is the authorization letter, Ex.P.2 is the cheque stands in the name of complainant company, Ex.P.3 is the endorsement issued by the bank stating dishonor of Ex.P.2 cheque, Ex.P.4 is the office copy of legal notice, Ex.P.5 is the postal receipt for having sent legal notice to the accused, Ex.P.6 is the Courier Receipt, Ex.P.7 is the Unserved postal cover and Ex.P.8 is the postal Track consignment and another Legal representative of complainant company is examined as PW.2 by filing his affidavit evidence in lieu of oral evidence, wherein, he has reiterated the entire averments made in the complaint.

In support of his evidence, PW.2 has produced a document as per Ex.P.9 is the Power of Attorney, Ex.P.10 is another Power of Attorney,
Ex.P.11 is the Statement of account and Ex.P.12 is the Certificate u/s 65(B) of Indian Evidence Act.
Thus, the complainant has complied the mandatory requirements of section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act.
Therefore, the presumptions can be drawn in his favour as contemplated U/s 118 and 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act.

9. Before proceed on the merits of the case, it is important to highlight the ingredients of Section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act and said Act has been enacted to lend credibility to the financial transactions.

sentences.text: (ii) Return of the cheque by the Bank as unpaid.
(iii) The drawer of the cheque fails to make the payment of the said amount within 15 days of the receipt of notice under the proviso (b) to Section 138.

The explanation appended to the section provides, that the debt or other liability, for the purpose of that section means a legally enforceable debt or other liability.
10.

Apart from this, Section 139 of Negotiable Instruments Act lays down a presumption in favour of the holder of cheque in the following terms;
"It shall be presumed unless the contrary is proved, that - the holder of the cheque received the cheque, of the nature referred to him section 138, for the discharge in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability."

11. On the other hand, to rebut the presumption accused himself examined as DW.1 and depose that,
he has not purchased any Tractor. One Nazeer who is residing at his adjoining village approached him and assured him that, someone will purchase the Tractor in the name of his wife and they will pay the entire loan amount.
Further he assured that, they will provide Rs.30,000/- for the said purpose.
As per the assurance given by the said Nazeer he has signed the loan documents.

Further,
he depose that, Tractor dealer himself came to Bagepalli and taken his signatures on cheque as well as other documents.
Further, he depose that, he went to police station to file complaint against said Nazeer but police have not taken his complaint.
SUBMISSION OF LEARNED COUNSEL FOR COMPLAINANT :
12. Learned counsel for complainant argued that, wife of the accused as well as accused himself approached the complainant for financial assistance of Rs.8,00,000/- to purchase vehicle.

Accordingly, complainant company sanctioned the loan but wife of the accused and accused failed to make periodical payments and against the outstanding amount accused being co-borrower issued a cheque which is marked at Ex.P.2 which on presentation was returned dishonored.
Further, she argued that, accused has not denied his signatures on the cheque and prayed to convict the accused.

SUBMISSION OF LEARNED COUNSEL FOR ACCUSED:
13.
On the other hand, learned counsel for accused argued that, complainant company has created the documents, accused never approached the complainant company for financial assistance.

In support of his arguments learned counsel for accused placed the reliance on Crl. Appeal No.
518/2006 between Krishna Janardhan Bhat Vs, Dattatraya G. Hedge.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for accused argued that, accused has not taken any loan amount and one Nazeer has insisted the accused to sign on the cheques and other documents, accused is innocent person and prays to consider the ground reality.
In support of his argument, he specifically relied upon the para No.34 of the above Judgment.

At para No.34 of the above Judgment Hon'ble Apex Court observed that, "We are not oblivious of the fact that the said provision has been inserted to regulate the growing business,

sentences.text: This, however, shall not mean that the courts shall put a blind eye to the ground realities.
Statute mandates raising of presumption but it stops at that.
It does not say how presumption drawn should be held to have rebutted.
Other important principles of legal jurisprudence, namely presumption of innocence as human rights and the doctrine of reverse burden introduced by Section 139 should be delicately balanced.
Such balancing acts, indisputably would largely depend upon the factual matrix of each case, the materials brought on record and having regard to legal principles governing the same".

ANALYSIS AND REASONING :
14. Having gone through the defence raised by the accused, he is not disputing the cheque in question and signature thereon are not belongs to him.
It is well settled that, when once the issuance of the cheque and signature is admitted, the presumption as contemplated U/s 139 of N. I. Act has to be raised in favour of the complainant.
The course open to the accused is to rebut the said presumption by raising a probable defence.

In this context of matter, it is useful to refer the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in APS FOREX SERVICES PRIVATE LTD., V/S SHAKTHI INTERNATIONAL FASHION LINKERS AND OTHERS reported in AIR 2020 Supreme Court 945,
wherein, it has been observed and held that once the issuance and the signature of the cheque/s is admitted, there is always presumption in favour of complainant that there exists legally enforceable debt or liability.

entities.text: APS FOREX SERVICES PRIVATE LTD., V/S SHAKTHI INTERNATIONAL FASHION LINKERS AND OTHERS reported in AIR 2020 Supreme Court 945
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 15. It is also profitable to refer another decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in P.RASIYA V/S ABDUL NAZEER AND ANOTHER reported in 2022 SCC Online Supreme Court 1131, wherein, it has been observed and held that once the initial burden is discharged by the complainant, that the cheque was issued by the accused and signature of the accused on the cheque is not disputed

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , then in that case, the onus will shift upon the accused to prove the contrary that the cheque was not for discharge or any debt or other liability.

16. There can be no dispute that, in matters relating to alleged offences U/s 138 of N. I. Act, the complainant has only to establish that, cheque was genuine, presented within time and upon it being dishonored, due notice was sent within 30 days of such dishonor, to which repayment must be received within 15 days, failing which a compliant can be filed within 01 month.

On the other hand,
the main defence available to the accused is to dispute and deny the repayment of the loan or liability to pay the amount for which the cheque was issued on the ground that, the said debt is not legally enforceable debt.
17. Admittedly in this case, accused admits his signature on the cheque.
As such, the presumption would arise U/s 139 of N. I. Act infavour of the complainant.
Now the next question that arise before this Court is that, Whether the accused had issued cheque in question for discharge of legally enforceable doubt?

sentences.text: In this case, accused has taken defence that, he has not issued any cheque to the complainant company.
But he has issued cheque to one Nazeer.
Having taken said defence accused failed to examine said Nazeer.

Though in his defence evidence he depose that, he went to police station to file complaint against said Nazeer but police have not taken his complaint, but in support of his defence he has not produced any document or adduce any evidence.
19. Apart, learned counsel for accused himself put a question to PW.1 that, complainant company has not read over any contents of the loan documents and to maintain good financial position

,
complainant company has extended the loan amount to the accused.

So, this itself shows that,
accused has availed the loan from the complainant.

On going through the evidence of the accused as well as cross-examination of PW.1, it reveals that, accused has raised different defenses during different stages of trial has clearly jeo-paralized the case of the accused and makes it highly doubtful.
20. Learned counsel for accused argued that, when the case is posted for argument, complainant has created and produced Ex.P.13 to Ex.P.15 documents.
On perusal of Ex.P.13 to 15 it reveals that, the said documents are loan applications and loan agreement pertaining to accused and his wife.
Even for the sake of discussion, if we exclude the said documents, accused himself in his evidence depose that, he has signed the loan documents.

In addition, as stated above, learned counsel for complainant himself put a question to PW.1 that, contents of the loan agreement not read over to the accused and to maintain good financial position, complainant company has sanctioned the loan.
Further, on perusal of Ex.P.11, it reveals that, accused has failed to repay the installment of amount properly to the complainant bank.
Cumulative effect of above discussion makes it clear that accused being co-barrower obtained the loan from the Complainant bank.
As such, in view of above discussion, question of creation of the documents at Ex.P.11 to 13 holds no water.

21. Learned Counsel for accused submitted that accused has not opened the account and transacted from the account which was/is relied by the complainant and to substantiate his say he relied upon Ex-D1.

On going through the said document ie Bank Statement standing in the name of the accused,
shows that since 29-12-2020 no transaction taken place.
That itself does not mean that accused has not availed the loan from the complainant bank.
Morever on perusal of Ex-P11 it revals that accused has taken the loan from the Complainant Company and accused has not re-paid loan amount as per the stipulated time.
22. Accused in the present case has maintained a defence that he had not issued the cheque in question to the complainant and he had issued the cheque to one Mr. Nazeer.
The defence of the Accused is mere averment and no material, leave alone, any cogent evidence, has been brought on record to substantiate the same.
It is a trite law that a bare denial by the Accused in his evidence would not assume the character of defence evidence.
Therefore, there is no evidence to rebut the presumption that the cheque was issued for consideration.
The Accused has to prove that there was no debt or liability towards the Complainant, mere denial is not sufficient.
S.20,87 and 139 of N. I.

Act when read in harmony, makes it clear that the drawer of the cheque is liable to pay unless the presumption has been rebutted by raising a probable defence and it would make no difference if the particulars of the cheque in question is filled by someone else if the cheque has been duly signed by the Accused.

sentences.text: Finally, counsel for accused argued that, demand notice is not served upon the accused.

But on perusal of postal track consignment i.e., Ex.P.6 and Postal cover i.e., Ex.P.7, it reveals that,
complainant has sent the legal notice i.e., Ex.P.4 o the accused through post and as per postal endorsement made on Ex.P.7 i.e., Postal Cover it reveals that "07 days party not in station".

Apart,
as per Sec.27 of General Clauses Act, once notice sent to the address of accused then it is deemed to be served on the accused.
Moreover, postal authority has not returned the cover by saying 'address not belongs to the accused'.
Further, DW.1/accused himself not disputed his address in his evidence.
Hence, argument by the learned counsel for accused in respect of non-service of demand notice is not acceptable.
24. Except denial accused has not placed any materials before the court to rebut the presumption available in favour of the complainant.
Finally, having considered the totality of facts and circumstances of the case, accused has failed to rebut the presumption infavour of the complainant as spelled U/s 139 of N. I. Act.
The law as laid down U/s 138 of N. I. Act is made out against the accused.
The weight of the evidence adduced by the complainant to prove his case against the accused is sufficient enough to impute criminality on the accused.
Complainant has successfully proved all the ingredients of Sec.138 of N. I. Act.
As such, the complainant has proved that there was loan transaction between the accused and the complainant and amount mentioned in the cheque is legally enforceable debt.
Accordingly, Point No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
25. POINT No.2:
Section 138 of N.I. Act empowers the Court to sentence the accused upto two years and also to impose fine which may extend to twice the amount of cheque or with both.
The cheque in question was issued on 16.12.2020 for Rs.3,45,000/-.
The complainant was deprived of money that was rightfully due to it for a period of almost 04 years 04 months.

So, having considered above facts and circumstances, if the interest is calculated at 9% p.a. on the cheques amount for the above period certainly the complainant is entitled for suitable compensation to the cheque amount as per Sec.80 of N. I. Act.

Hence, in this case Rs.3,45,000/- is the cheque amount and interest at 9% for 04 years 04 months if calculated will amounts to Rs.1,34,550/- as the case is pending about 52 months and as such the total amount including interest will be of Rs.4,79,550/-.
26. However, having regard to the facts of the case and the amount involved, there are no warranting circumstances to award the sentence of imprisonment as substantive sentence.
Directing the accused to pay fine and also awarding compensation to the complainant would meet the ends of justice.
But adequate default sentence shall have to be imposed to ensure the recovery of fine imposed to the accused.
Therefore, the complainant is required to be suitably compensated as per Section 80 and 117 of the Negotiable Instrument Act and also appropriate in default sentence.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER Acting U/Sec.255(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused is found guilty for the offence punishable under Sec.138 of N. I. Act and he is sentenced to pay a fine of Rs.4,79,550/- (Rupees four lakh seventy nine thousand five hundred and fifty Only).
In default to pay fine
, the accused shall undergo simple imprisonment for a period of six months.
